set.body:
Objective:
Define Frame semantics independently of every optional engine and implement the always-available small JVM/Scala.js reference interpreter over scoped record batches. This interpreter is a semantic oracle and testing backend, not a production columnar engine.

Semantic constitution:
- SQL-style three-valued logic; filters retain only true.
- Null equality, null-safe equality, grouping of null keys, NaN behavior, integer overflow, casts, timestamp units/zones, dictionary equality, collation, sort stability, and floating reduction policy are explicit.
- There is no hidden row index. Keys are ordinary columns. Order is represented by an inspectable OrderGuarantee and preserved only by operators whose contract says so.
- Backend equivalence means these semantics, with any permitted floating-order tolerance declared in the plan or receipt.

Execution boundary:
- The reference interpreter owns only the minimal kernels required to establish semantics; it does not pursue a production optimizer, spill system, SIMD framework, or pandas-scale operation catalog.
- Query construction and logical explain are pure.
- Resource-safe execution exposes FS2 streams of scoped RecordBatch values. Collecting resource-backed results is Resource-scoped; an explicitly owned copying convenience may return F[OwnedTable].
- Plans contain immutable source descriptions. Execution scopes readers, buffers, cancellation, early termination, and failures.
- Project, filter, and limit stream without whole-input materialization. Blocking behavior and memory estimates are inspectable before execution.
- Backend physical explain is separate from pure logical explain and reports accepted pushdown, buffering, and copies.

Acceptance:
- Project, withColumn, filter, limit, expression evaluation, null handling, and baseline reductions execute on JVM and Scala.js.
- Deterministic fixtures and property laws cover three-valued logic, filter composition, projection identity, ordering guarantees, chunk-boundary invariance, checked arithmetic, and structured failures.
- Stream cancellation, early termination, failed actions, and collection close all acquired resources.
- Explain output distinguishes logical and normalized plans from interpreter-specific physical execution.
- No engine silently changes semantics or falls back to another backend.
- Performance receipts characterize representative primitive and UTF-8 paths without presenting the reference interpreter as a production competitor.
